question.text: Will at least one additional U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before July 1, 2027, a U.S. state without an existing cage-free law in effect as of September 1, 2026, enacts a new cage-free requirement.

A cage-free requirement is a law or rule that either bans the use of cages for in-state hens or bans the sale of eggs from non-cage-free hens.
question.fine_print:
To qualify, a cage-free requirement may be enacted by the state legislature, passed by a ballot measure, or implemented via state administrative action. The requirement need not come into effect before July 1, 2027.

If a state legislature passes a cage-free requirement, that will suffice for this question to resolve as Yes, regardless of the action or inaction of the state's governor.

States with cage-free requirement on the books as of September 15, 2026 are Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah, and Washington.

research:
# Will another U.S. state enact a cage-free egg requirement before July 2027? Research brief

I found no sign that this has already resolved. No new state has enacted a cage-free requirement in 2023, 2024, 2025 or 2026 so far. The trend since 2024 has been delays, suspensions and court losses, and every bill I found in a non-listed state was stalled. Almost all the remaining window falls in the 2027 legislative sessions, which start in January.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question names no data series or URL. It comes down to state legislative, ballot or administrative records. The named list of states with existing laws (as of 2026-09-15) is Arizona, California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Michigan, Nevada, Oregon, Rhode Island, Utah and Washington.
- 2026 (page footer, no update date): The ASPCA's state confinement-ban page lists the same 10 states for laying hens. Its latest dated changes are the 2025 Arizona delay, the 2025 Nevada suspension provision, and the 2024 Rhode Island and Utah delays to 2030. It shows no new state. [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/improving-laws-animals/public-policy/farm-animal-confinement-bans)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles the question. I found no new state enacting a cage-free law in 2026 and no statewide cage-free ballot measure on the November 2026 ballot.
- 2026-01-07: New York's A652, a cage-free housing requirement, was referred to the Assembly Agriculture Committee. That was its only 2026 action. The Senate companion, S950, shows no 2026 vote. The 2025-26 session ends 2026-12-31, so these bills die and would have to be reintroduced in 2027. [NY Senate A652](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/A652), [S950](https://www.nysenate.gov/legislation/bills/2025/S950)
- Illinois: the only 2026 hen bill I found, HB4764, is about backyard chickens, not commercial cage-free housing. It was re-referred to the Rules Committee on 2026-03-27. [ILGA](https://www.ilga.gov/Legislation/BillStatus?DocTypeID=HB&DocNum=4764&GAID=18&SessionID=114&LegID=165897)
- I did not find any bills pre-filed for 2027.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: A Maricopa County judge, Scott Blaney, struck down Arizona's cage-free rule. He held that the Department of Agriculture lacked specific authority to require cage-free housing. The Attorney General's office is "reviewing" the decision. Humane World for Animals said it would push for a new law or a future ballot measure. Arizona is already on the named list, so it is unclear whether a new Arizona law would count. [KJZZ](https://www.kjzz.org/business/2026-11-03/arizona-judge-rules-against-cage-free-requirements-for-egg-producers)
- Early November 2026: Advocates reported wins on animal ballot measures in the midterms, such as foie gras measures in DC and Denver. None was a statewide hen measure. [Optimist Daily](https://www.optimistdaily.com/2026/11/animal-welfare-ballot-measures-had-a-strong-night-in-the-2026-midterms/), [Animals 24-7](https://www.animals24-7.org/2026/11/05/more-wins-for-animals-on-election-night-2026-than-anyone-can-drink-to/)
- 2026-10-07: A federal judge dismissed the Justice Department's January 2026 lawsuit against Michigan's cage-free law for lack of standing. A similar federal suit against California was also dismissed. I found no report of an appeal. [Michigan Public](https://www.michiganpublic.org/politics-government/2026-10-13/federal-lawsuit-against-michigans-cage-free-egg-law-thrown-out-by-judge), [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/policy/judge-rejects-doj-suit-against-michigan-cage-free-egg-law)
- September 2026: The Senate Agriculture Committee passed a Farm Bill without the "Save Our Bacon" language that would override state laws like California's Prop 12. The House version (passed in late April 2026) includes it as Section 12006, so a conference fight is still pending. [Animal Equality](https://animalequality.org/news/2026/05/05/us-house-passes-farm-bill/), [Spectrum](https://spectrumlocalnews.com/nc/triad/politics/2026/09/21/pork-producers-plead-for-prop--12--fix--as-lawmakers-make-progress-on-farm-bill)
- 2026-01-22: The Justice Department sued Michigan, arguing the federal Egg Products Inspection Act overrides its law. That signals federal hostility to state cage-free mandates. [Civil Eats](https://civileats.com/2026/01/28/trump-doj-sues-michigan-to-overturn-cage-free-egg-law/)

## 4. Base rates
- When each listed state first enacted a requirement: California 2008/2010, Washington 2011, Massachusetts 2016, Rhode Island 2018, Oregon 2019, Michigan 2019, Colorado 2020, Nevada 2021, Utah 2021, Arizona 2022 (an agency rule). That is about 9 new states from 2016 to 2022, roughly 1.3 a year. [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/improving-laws-animals/public-policy/farm-animal-confinement-bans)
- Since 2023 there have been zero new states in about 4 years. Over the same period the movement went backwards:
  - 2024: Rhode Island and Utah delayed their laws to 2030.
  - 2025: Arizona delayed its rule to 2034.
  - 2025: Nevada gave itself power to suspend its sales ban, and did suspend it from 2025-02-20.
  - Repeal bills were filed in Michigan and Colorado; the Colorado one died. [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/agribusiness-news/some-states-back-off-cage-free-mandates-during-bird-flu-crisis), [Animal Ag Alliance](https://animalagalliance.org/egg-prices-cage-free-mandates-legislation/)
- Bills in New York, Maryland (for example SB806 in 2025), Illinois (SB3655 in 2024) and Hawaii (2022-23) all died in committee. [LegiScan MD SB806](https://legiscan.com/MD/bill/SB806/2025), [WATTAgNet](https://www.wattagnet.com/egg/cage-free-laying-systems/article/15665030/cagefree-law-proposed-in-illinois-legislature)

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus market on new state cage-free laws.
- The Kalshi markets collected for this brief are not relevant. For example, there is a market on whether Cal-Maine will say "Cage-Free" on its 2027-01-06 earnings call (0.80), plus egg-price markets. None of them measures state legislation.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- January to June 2027: Most state legislatures meet. New York, New Jersey, Maryland, Illinois, Hawaii and Vermont are the likeliest places for bills, but I found no 2027 filings yet. Advocacy groups have been focused on defending existing laws.
- Late 2026 to 2027: Farm Bill conference. If the "Save Our Bacon" language survives, it would weaken the case for new state laws. As reported, the House text may not cover hens; one source says it excludes egg-laying hens. [Stateline](https://stateline.org/2026/06/03/animal-welfare-rules-might-be-rolled-back-by-congress/)
- Possible appeals: the Arizona ruling, and the Justice Department's dismissed suit against Michigan.
- Egg prices and bird flu: high prices have driven the recent delays and repeal attempts.
- No statewide ballot measure can be enacted before July 2027. The next general election is November 2028, so an earlier measure would need a special election.

I found no qualifying event. No new state has adopted a cage-free requirement since 2021, and every state-level move I found in 2025-2026 went the other way: delays, suspensions or repeal attempts.

I found no final deal as of November. [Farm and Dairy](https://www.farmanddairy.com/news/senate-releases-draft-farm-bill-cuts-save-our-bacon-act/920581.html); [Humane World](https://www.humaneworld.org/en/news/whats-happening-california-prop-12-farm-bill-save-our-bacon-act)

- 2026-03-20: a federal judge dismissed DOJ's suit against California's egg laws for lack of standing. A similar DOJ suit against Michigan (filed Jan 2026) was reportedly also dismissed for standing. [CA AG](https://oag.ca.gov/node/620511); [Feedstuffs](https://www.feedstuffs.com/policy/judge-rejects-doj-suit-against-michigan-cage-free-egg-law)
- 2025: Arizona's governor delayed the state's rule (to 2034 per ASPCA, 2032 per Brooks Institute) and vetoed the SB1721 repeal on 2025-04-18. Nevada passed a law allowing emergency suspension. Utah moved to extend its deadline. Repeal bills in Colorado and Michigan failed. [ASPCA](https://www.aspca.org/news/what-lawmakers-did-farm-animals-2025); [Brooks Institute](https://thebrooksinstitute.org/animal-law-digest/us/issue-294/arizona-governor-vetoes-bill-blocking-cage-free-egg-requirements-supports-rule-delay-implementation); [KSL](https://www.ksl.com/article/50878335/utah-committee-advances-bill-to-eggs-tend-states-cage-free-hen-law-deadline-)

- That is about 10 states over 2008-2021, mostly clustered in 2016-2021 when advocates were pushing hard. Since 2021 (about 5 years) there have been zero new states. After the bird-flu price spikes of 2022-25, the direction reversed.
- Earlier bills in New York (several sessions), Illinois (SB3655 died 2025-01-07), Maryland (2024 bill "cracked under pressure") and Hawaii (HB538/SB346, outcome not found) all failed. [ILGA](https://ilga.gov/legislation/BillStatus.asp?DocNum=3655&DocTypeID=SB&GA=103&GAID=17&LegId=153601&SessionID=112); [Cecil Whig](https://www.cecildaily.com/news/state_news/cage-free-egg-bill-cracks-under-pressure/article_bbb1f3e0-e7cc-11ee-adf9-dbf6978dfc4a.html)

- January-June 2027 sessions: most legislatures convene in January. New York runs through about June and is the most likely place for a reintroduced cage-free bill. New Jersey and Illinois also have full-length sessions. I found no 2027 cage-free bills prefiled anywhere.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) Time left and what Yes requires: The window runs from now (2026-11-18) to July 1, 2027, about 7.5 months, and nearly all of it falls in the January to June 2027 legislative sessions. Yes requires a state outside the ten listed (AZ, CA, CO, MA, MI, NV, OR, RI, UT, WA) to enact a cage-free requirement before July 1, 2027. That can happen by legislative passage (governor action not needed), a ballot measure, or an agency rule, and it can cover either in-state hens or egg sales.

(b) Status quo: No. No new state has adopted such a law since the Arizona rule in 2022. No bills are prefiled for 2027 in any non-listed state, and no statewide ballot measures can be voted on before July 2027.

(c) Base rate: From 2016 to 2022 about 1.3 new states were added per year, which would imply roughly 50-60% over a half-year session window. That reference period ended about four years ago. Since 2023 there have been zero new states in about four sessions, and the trend has reversed. For the current regime, a fair base rate is about 5-10% per session year.

(d) Evidence:
- For Yes:
  - The DOJ suits against California (dismissed 2026-03-20) and Michigan (dismissed 2026-10-07) both failed, which removes some legal uncertainty.
  - The Senate farm bill (September 2026) dropped the Save Our Bacon preemption.
  - Several Democratic-trifecta states (NY, NJ, IL, MD, HI, VT) remain plausible venues, and advocacy groups are motivated after strong 2026 midterm ballot results.
- For No:
  - NY S950/A652 died in committee in 2026.
  - Maryland (2024, 2025), Illinois (2024) and Hawaii bills all died.
  - Rhode Island and Utah delayed their laws in 2024. Arizona delayed in 2025, and its rule was struck down on 2026-11-03. Nevada suspended its sales ban on 2025-02-20.
  - Nevada SB41, a repeal, was prefiled on 2026-11-09.
  - Bird flu and egg-price politics continue to favor rollback, and advocates are focused on defending existing laws.

(e) Scenarios:
- No: New York reintroduces its bill and it again sits in the Agriculture committee. Other states see no movement, and the 2027 sessions end with zero new laws.
- Yes: Egg prices ease, and New Jersey or New York pushes through a cage-free sales bill late in session, perhaps paired with a delayed effective date such as 2032. Alternatively, a small state like Vermont passes an in-state housing rule with little opposition.

(f) Adjustment: I start at about 8% for one session year in the current regime. I move down for the absence of any prefiled bills, the continuing rollback momentum, and advocates' defensive posture. I move slightly up for the edge cases: a narrow law covering only in-state hens would count, and governor action is not needed. There is no matching prediction market to anchor on. My final estimate is about 5%.

Probability: 5%

(a) The forecast closes 2026-12-18 and the question is scheduled to resolve around 2026-12-31, but the qualifying window runs to July 1, 2027. If resolution happens at end-2026, only about 6 weeks remain, mostly outside legislative sessions. If the full window applies, the January-June 2027 sessions matter. For Yes, a state not on the list (AZ, CA, CO, MA, MI, NV, OR, RI, UT, WA) must enact a cage-free requirement before July 1, 2027. That can be a legislature passing a bill (the governor's action is irrelevant), a ballot measure, or an agency rule.

(b) Status quo: No. No new state has enacted a requirement since 2021-22, and no bills are pending or prefiled.

(c) Base rate: from 2016 to 2022 about 1.3 states a year adopted requirements. Since 2022 the count is zero over about 4-5 years, and the movement has gone backwards. Using the recent regime (0 in about 4.5 years, Laplace-smoothed), the chance of a new state in a roughly 7-month window is about 10%. Adjusted for the current rollback environment, it is lower, about 5%.

(d) Evidence for No:
- New York's S950/A652 died in committee in 2026 (roundup dated 2026-07-09).
- No 2027 cage-free bills are prefiled anywhere.
- Nevada SB41, prefiled 2026-11-09, would repeal Nevada's provisions.
- Delays came in RI and UT (2024) and AZ (2025), and Nevada suspended its sales ban in 2025.
- Arizona's rule was struck down on 2026-11-03.
- The DOJ has been hostile (Michigan suit, January 2026).
- The House-passed Save Our Bacon preemption is still pending in conference.
- No statewide ballot measures are possible before July 2027.

Evidence for Yes:
- The DOJ suits against California (2026-03-20) and Michigan (2026-10-07) were dismissed.
- Advocates won some animal ballot measures in November 2026.
- Humane World says it will pursue new Arizona legislation, but Arizona is on the list and its legislature is Republican.
- Full-time Democratic legislatures (NY, NJ, IL) could move a bill in 2027.

(e) No scenario: the 2027 sessions focus on egg prices and bird flu, cage-free bills are reintroduced in NY and NJ but stall in committee, and the Farm Bill fight discourages new state mandates.

Yes scenario: the NJ or NY legislature, with egg prices easing, passes a cage-free sales ban in June 2027 after advocacy groups refocus on expansion.

(f) I start from about 5-10% and adjust down for three reasons: the absence of any pending vehicle, the reversed policy trend, and the possibility that resolution effectively happens at end-2026 with almost no time left. Some tail risk remains from full-time legislatures and from ambiguity over which states count. I land at about 3-4%.

Probability: 3%

(a) There are about 7.5 months left, from 2026-11-18 to 2027-07-01. The real window is the January to June 2027 legislative sessions. Legislative passage alone counts, even without the governor's signature. Arizona re-enacting after its court loss would likely not count, since it had a law in effect as of 2026-09-01.

(b) Status quo is No. No new state has acted since 2022, and no bills are pre-filed for 2027.

(c) Base rate:

(d) Evidence:
- **For Yes:**
  - Federal suits against the California and Michigan laws were dismissed (2026-03-20 and 2026-10-07), which removes some legal cloud.

  - New York's bills died in committee in 2026.

  - Nevada SB41 was pre-filed in November 2026 to repeal its law.
  - The DOJ is hostile, and bird flu and egg prices remain salient.
  - No ballot route is available before July 2027.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** New York reintroduces its bill, but it stalls in the Agriculture committees. No other state moves, and advocates spend 2027 defending Arizona, Nevada and Michigan. This is very likely.
- **Yes:** A Democratic trifecta state, such as New Jersey, Maryland, Delaware or Hawaii, passes a cage-free sales bill in spring 2027, possibly with a long phase-in. That becomes feasible now that much of the industry has already transitioned and the federal suits have failed.

(f) I start at about 6% and move down slightly because:
- The trend is negative.
- Nothing is pre-filed.
- Advocacy is focused on defense.

I keep a small tail for a surprise legislative passage, since passage alone counts. There is no matching prediction market to anchor on.
